text:
Sam: quick sync — acme's legal wants p95 120ms and p99 480ms for their doc-chat flow. sales looped in Priya/Marco to confirm willingness to pay for dedicated vs hosted :thinking_face:
Priya: they're firm on p95 120ms. p99 is negotiable but they'd like <500ms. they also asked if we can guarantee this without dedicated for first 3 months.
Marco: Selling point is predictable tail. customer prefers hosted first, then dedicated if traffic grows. we need clear failure modes + cost delta for sales deck.
Tasha: short notes from runtime perspective:
- current default kernel path for the model (mpt-30b-qlora-ish) uses int8-ffn + fused_attention on A100s
- microbatch_size=8 looks good for throughput, but raises median/p95 when KV warmup cold
- KV cache warmup: cold starts add ~70-120ms on p99 for long dialogues
- observed a small perf regression on last release: p99 increased ~30-40ms for requests with >1024 tokens
Sam: can you paste the profiling snippet? trying to make tradeoff table for Priya/Marco
Tasha: sure — here's abbreviated trace (from perf-run-2026-03-15):
```
trace: request_id=abc123
- accept/parse: 6ms
- routing & policy: 3ms
- kernel dispatch: 14ms
- kv lookup (cold): 95ms
- attention + ffn kernels: 48ms
- postprocess: 4ms
= total ~170ms (p50 ~90ms, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~360ms for this class)
```
Tasha: warm KV snapshot (kept alive) drops kv lookup to ~12ms -> total p99 ~280-300ms. so warmup matters a lot.
Priya: ok — two levers for SLAs: require dedicated with pinned warmup (we claim p99<350ms) OR hosted but with a start-up SLA (first N requests per call may exceed p99) and higher price.
Marco: customer will push for hosted. what's the pricing delta for guaranteed warm KV vs best-effort?
Sam: need a quick cost estimate. Tasha, can you quantify GPU-hours / memory overhead for always-warmed KV per customer?
Tasha: warm KV requires ~2GB persistent KV per model instance and costs about 0.07 GPU-hours per 1k qps-hour due to pinned instances (rough ballpark). for acme (expected 50 qps steady) that's ~3.36 GPU-hours/day -> ballpark $x/day (I'll refine).
Priya: also highlight fallback behavior: if capacity constrained we can route to cheaper quant kernel (smaller memory) but that increases p99 ~+60-90ms and degrades quality slightly. need to document quality delta for sales.
Sam: we should prepare two concrete offer lines:
1) Hosted standard: p95 120ms, p99 best effort (<800ms), no warm pinned KV, lower price.
2) Hosted premium (pinned warm KV): p95 120ms, p99 <350ms, higher price, can be a 3-month pilot.
Marco: agree. also flag the perf regression — is it a kernel or scheduler issue?
Tasha: looks like a scheduler bump combined with fallback to less-optimized FFN kernel for >1024 tokens. I bisected and found a configuration change in microbatcher -> changed from dynamic to static microbatch sharding which increased queuing for long sequences.
Sam: can we revert that change or make it conditional?
Tasha: revert for now on canary, and add a conditional path: if seq_len>1024 -> prefer fused_ffn path even if it sacrifices some memory. I'll open a small PR.
deploy-bot: canary rollback deployed to canary cluster at 1723456799 by Tasha (link: https://deploys.redwood.local/deploy/1723456799) :white_check_mark:
Tasha: perf after rollback on canary: p99 for >1024 requests dropped ~38ms and kv-cold still the dominant factor. will add KV prewarm hook to the request router so we can prefetch KV during initial TLS handshake for long-running sessions.
Priya: for sales narrative, please give one-sentence impact statements: how much delta in p99 if customer opts out of pinned KV, and what microbatch setting we recommend as default for hosted premium.
Tasha: two lines: "Opting out of pinned KV increases p99 by ~150-200ms for long dialogues; enabling pinned KV keeps p99 within 300-350ms." and "Recommend microbatch_size=4 for hosted premium (reduces p95 slightly but improves tail stability)"
Sam: nice. Marco/Priya — do you want a short slide with numbers and the canary perf graph for tomorrow's call?
Marco: yes please. include cost delta, warmup behavior, and fallback quality notes.
Priya: i'll own slide deck. Sam/Tasha send final numbers by EOD.
Tasha: will upload refined numbers and a small CSV of perf runs (warm vs cold, mb=4/8/16, kernels int8/fp16) before EOD.
Sam: thanks team. follow-ups: Tasha -> PR to revert canary change + KV prewarm hook (ETA 4h). Priya -> slides + customer messaging. Marco -> pricing sketch.
Priya: also loop legal on required SLA language, suggest language for 'best-effort p99' vs 'guaranteed p99' carveouts.
Sam: noted. if anything blocks, ping here. :rocket:
